intent: Record as reviewed the login, session, operator and dev-login rules the identity Context enforces and tests.
observable_outcome: get-context identity lists the rules as reviewed, each proven by its test.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A GitHub login callback is refused with 401 before any code exchange unless its state matches the state cookie set when the login began.
A session counts only strictly before its expiry; at the expiry instant it is already signed out.
An unexpired session stops counting once its account is being purged or has been deleted.
An operator route lets a request through only for a user on the operator roster; anyone else gets 404 and a refused signed-in user is audited.
The development login route exists only when development login is enabled; otherwise it answers 404.
A development login name longer than 64 characters is refused with 400 before any account is touched.
The Workspace carried by a signed-in request is reused only when asking about its own owner; any other account's Workspace is read from its owner.
When the GitHub profile carries no email, the login uses only the address GitHub marks both primary and verified.
GitHub rate limiting, server errors and transport failures answer 503, while other GitHub refusals answer 401, so an outage never reads as a bad credential.
A GitHub login whose profile carries no email is refused when no address is both primary and verified, so an unverified address can never claim an account.
